desc: CUFON was, from 1983, the first electronic public archive of US government UFO documents - a dial-up bulletin board in Seattle operated by Dale Goudie and Jim Klotz that published FOIA releases in full text at a time when the alternative was mail-order photocopies. Its editorial method anticipated the modern document-first approach: publish the agency's own paper, with the FOIA case number, and let the reader judge. CUFON's most consequential work was on the NSA holdings and the CAUS litigation record, and on the 1975 SAC overflight documents, where it circulated the NORAD and command-post message traffic that transformed those incidents from anecdote into records. It is the direct ancestor of The Black Vault, and it established the norm - now standard in this field - that the useful unit of evidence is a released document with a traceable case number rather than a witness account.
